name: Efficient training with fewer parameters
gist: These papers make fine-tuning much cheaper by only updating a small part of a model instead of all weights, using rank-based tricks or clever decompositions.
explain: Modern language models are pretrained on billions of words, which costs millions of dollars. But then you want to adapt them for your specific task — legal documents, medical records, custom domains. If you retrain all the weights, you need almost as much compute as the original training. What if you could fine-tune the model by updating only a tiny fraction of its weights? These papers tackle that problem. Methods like Low-Rank Adaptation add a small, low-rank matrix (a grid of numbers with special structure) that sits alongside the pretrained weights and gets trained instead of changing the weights directly. It is like putting a thin filter over the network that learns the new task, while the core knowledge stays frozen.

Why does this work? Because the weight updates actually live in a lower-dimensional space. When you train a model, the changes to the weights do not point randomly in all directions — they move along a few important directions that capture the task you are learning. If you can identify and train only those directions, you do far less work. The catch is figuring out which directions matter and how to structure the small trainable part so it can still express everything the model needs to learn.

Another angle is adapter modules — small neural networks bolted onto existing layers that learn the new task, leaving the pretrained weights alone. These papers compare different structures: matrices, adapters, prefix-tuning (adding extra text chunks that get trained), and combinations. They measure how many weights you need to update versus how well the model performs on new tasks. The goal is to make fine-tuning cheap enough that individuals and small companies can adapt large models without needing a supercomputer.

papers.title: CR-Net: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Training with Cross-Layer Low-Rank Structure
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art low-rank frameworks across model scales from 60M to 7B parameters while requiring fewer computational resources and less memory.

papers.title: Decoupled Low-Rank Adaptation for Robust Federated Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various noisy federated scenarios by establishing global consensus through aggregating B while preserving local feature alignment.

papers.title: LoFT: Low-Rank Adaptation That Behaves Like Full Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: LoFT substantially narrows performance gap with full fine-tuning, consistently outperforms LoRA without increasing inference cost and eliminates hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: LoRA-DA: Data-Aware Initialization for Low-Rank Adaptation via Asymptotic Analysis
papers.contribution: Consistently improves final accuracy over existing LoRA initialization methods with faster convergence and robustness across ranks.

papers.title: QWHA: Quantization-Aware Walsh-Hadamard Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in low-bit quantization accuracy and achieves significant training speedups over existing Fourier-based adapters.

papers.title: SHINE: A Scalable In-Context Hypernetwork for Mapping Context to LoRA in a Single Pass
papers.contribution: SHINE generates LoRA adapters without fine-tuning, enabling complex question-answering tasks by transforming in-context knowledge to in-parameter knowledge in one pass while greatly saving time, computation, and memory.

papers.title: Thicker and Quicker: The Jumbo Token for Fast Plain Vision Transformers
papers.contribution: Improves ViT baselines at Nano-Large scales while maintaining speed; gains 4.9% on MAE pre-training, 5.2% on test-time adaptation, compatible with ViT methods.

papers.title: Weight Updates as Activation Shifts: A Principled Framework for Steering
papers.contribution: Achieves accuracy within 0.2%-0.9% of full-parameter tuning on average across tasks and models while training only 0.04% of parameters, outperforming ReFT and LoRA.

papers.title: AutoQRA: Joint Optimization of Mixed-Precision Quantization and Low-rank Adapters for Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Achieves performance close to full-precision fine-tuning under given memory budgets through intelligent configuration search.

papers.title: BoRA: Towards More Expressive Low-Rank Adaptation with Block Diversity
papers.contribution: BoRA increases LoRA rank expressiveness by factor b with minimal parameter overhead, demonstrating superior performance across multiple datasets and models.

papers.title: CLIMB: Taming the LoRA Residency Cliff in Multi-LoRA Serving
papers.contribution: Averts residency cliff collapse, reducing VIP TTFT p99 from 38.7 s to 13.1 s at matched throughput by shifting fetch-induced stalls to managed ingress queues.

papers.title: COSA: Context-aware Output-Space Adapter for Test-Time Adaptation in Time Series Forecasting
papers.contribution: Across diverse scenarios, COSA demonstrates substantial performance gains versus baselines without TTA (13

papers.title: Compress then Merge: From Multiple LoRAs into One Low-Rank Adapter
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms existing single-LoRA-output baselines while guaranteeing rank-r by construction and narrowing performance gap to full-parameter merging.

papers.title: Diving into Kronecker Adapters: Component Design Matters
papers.contribution: Component configuration guidelines and practical stabilization enable Kronecker adapters to better align with full fine-tuning across various architectures and modalities.

papers.title: Do We Need Adam? Surprisingly Strong and Sparse Reinforcement Learning with SGD in LLMs
papers.contribution: SGD matches or outperforms AdamW in RL for LLMs while updating fewer than 0.02% of model parameters (over 1000× fewer than AdamW) without sparsity regularization.

papers.title: Doc-to-LoRA: Learning to Instantly Internalize Contexts
papers.contribution: On long-context tasks, D2L achieves near-perfect zero-shot accuracy at sequence lengths exceeding the target LLM's native context window by 4× while reducing latency and memory.

papers.title: Efficient Discriminative Joint Encoders for Large Scale Vision-Language Reranking
papers.contribution: EDJE processes 50k image-text pairs/second with 49kB disk storage per image while matching prior art on Flickr and COCO retrieval benchmarks.

papers.title: Efficient Orthogonal Fine-Tuning with Principal Subspace Adaptation
papers.contribution: PSOFT achieves semantic preservation, expressiveness, and multi-dimensional efficiency simultaneously across 35 NLP and CV tasks on four representative models.

papers.title: Evaluating Parameter Efficient Methods for RLVR
papers.contribution: The work provides definitive guidance for parameter-efficient RL methods, demonstrating that structural variants like DoRA and AdaLoRA consistently outperform standard LoRA.

papers.title: E²LoRA: Efficient and Effective Low-Rank Adaptation with Entropy-Guided Adaptive Sharing
papers.contribution: E²LoRA achieves an excellent balance of efficiency and effectiveness, consistently matching or surpassing baselines with approximately 50% fewer trainable parameters across diverse tasks and modalities.

papers.title: FedRot-LoRA: Mitigating Rotational Misalignment in Federated LoRA
papers.contribution: Convergence analysis shows alignment yields tighter aggregation error bounds; consistently outperforms baselines across heterogeneity levels without restricting expressivity.

papers.title: Federated Sketching LoRA: A Flexible Framework for Heterogeneous Collaborative Fine-Tuning of LLMs
papers.contribution: FSLoRA provides convergence analysis showing how sketching ratios affect convergence rate, and empirically demonstrates improved training efficiency while preserving stable convergence.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning of Transformer models with Frames
papers.contribution: Achieves performance comparable to or exceeding state-of-the-art PEFT techniques while requiring far fewer trainable parameters and reduced memory footprint.

papers.title: FlexLoRA: Entropy-Guided Flexible Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.contribution: FlexLoRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

papers.title: GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry
papers.contribution: Matches or outperforms state-of-the-art with only 0.29% storage and 25% computational time under the same selection budget.

papers.title: Gradient Intrinsic Dimensionality Alignment：Narrowing The Gap Between Low-Rank Adaptation and Full Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Achieves over 5% improvement on GLUE, +0.57 on MT-Bench, +5.23% on GSM8K, +5.69% on HumanEval, and +1.58% on image classification.

papers.title: LRAgent: Efficient KV Cache Sharing for Multi-LoRA LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Achieves throughput and latency close to fully shared caching while preserving accuracy near non-shared baseline across agentic question-answering.

papers.title: LearniBridge: Learnable Calibration of Feature Caching for Diffusion Models Acceleration
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 5.87x acceleration on FLUX, 5.75x on HunyuanVideo, and 4.10x on WAN 2.1 with minimal quality loss.

papers.title: Learning Rate Scaling across LoRA Ranks and Transfer to Full Finetuning
papers.contribution: Identifies a configuration enabling learning rate transfer from LoRA to full finetuning, drastically reducing tuning costs across language, vision, and RL tasks.

papers.title: Learning in the Fisher Subspace: A Guided Initialization for LoRA Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Data-aware initialization consistently and significantly improves downstream performance across diverse tasks and modalities compared to existing approaches.

papers.title: LiME: Lightweight Mixture of Experts for Efficient Multimodal Multi-task Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive or superior performance on MMT-47 (47 multimodal tasks) while using 4x fewer parameters and 29% faster training compared to MoE-PEFT baselines.

papers.title: Memba: Membrane-driven Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mamba
papers.contribution: Memba achieves substantial improvements over existing PEFT methods across language and vision tasks.

papers.title: MiSS: Revisiting the Trade-off in LoRA with an Efficient Shard-Sharing Structure
papers.contribution: MiSS reduces optimization complexity while maintaining strong performance and achieving favorable balance between performance, memory, and efficiency.

papers.title: On-the-Fly Adaptation to Quantization: Configuration-Aware LoRA for Efficient Fine-Tuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.contribution: CoA-LoRA achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art methods without additional time cost, enabling efficient adaptation to arbitrary quantization configurations.

papers.title: Optimizing Inference-Time Compute for Medical Reasoning via Uncertainty Quantification
papers.contribution: Reduces inference token consumption by 4.7x to 6.4x on Qwen and Llama respectively, with minimal performance trade-offs while naturally producing distinct non-thinking and thinking modes.

papers.title: PLoP: Precise LoRA Placement for Efficient Finetuning of Large Models
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms or competes with commonly used LoRA placement strategies on supervised finetuning and reinforcement learning for reasoning tasks.

papers.title: PRAC: Principal-Random Subspace for LLM Activation Compression and Memory-Efficient Training
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 36% total memory reduction with negligible performance degradation and minimal computational cost on pre-training and fine-tuning tasks.

papers.title: QeRL: Beyond Efficiency - Quantization-enhanced Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
papers.contribution: Achieved 1.2x-1.5x speedup over BF16 LoRA and 1.5x-2.0x over QLoRA while reducing memory, enabling 32B LLM training on single H100 GPU.

papers.title: SSR-Merge: Subspace Signal Routing for Training-Free LoRA Merging in Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: SSR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods with proven mathematical optimality via OLS solution and streaming algorithm with reduced memory overhead.

papers.title: STAR: Rethinking MoE Routing as Structure-Aware Subspace Learning
papers.contribution: STAR consistently improves routing quality and downstream performance on large-scale language and vision tasks with optional test-time subspace updates for robustness.

papers.title: ScaLoRA: Optimally Scaled Low-Rank Adaptation for Efficient High-Rank Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Consistent performance gains and faster convergence relative to LoRA variants on NLU, reasoning, and math tasks up to 12B parameters.

papers.title: SliceFine: The Universal Winning-Slice Hypothesis for Pretrained Networks
papers.contribution: Matches SOTA PEFT methods while significantly improving training speed, memory efficiency, and model compactness across language and vision tasks.

papers.title: Stabilizing Native Low-Rank LLM Pretraining
papers.contribution: LLMs can be trained from scratch using exclusively low-rank weights without full-rank guidance, establishing compute-optimal scaling laws for low-rank transformers with improved inference efficiency.

papers.title: TRAC: Tensor-Train based Across-layer Compression for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: TRAC achieves performance comparable to LoRA variants while substantially reducing trainable parameters and storage requirements across diverse architectures.

papers.title: TopAdapter: Topology-Aware Prompt Tuning for Efficient Point Cloud Understanding
papers.contribution: TopAdapter outperforms existing PEFT methods and achieves performance comparable to full fine-tuning across point cloud benchmarks.

papers.title: xKV: Cross-Layer KV-Cache Compression via Aligned Singular Vector Extraction
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 8x KV-Cache compression and 4.23x end-to-end speedup while preserving accuracy on long-context tasks.
